o1.biggest_strength: It uses all three data signals and checks the numbers: writing weighted heaviest, an overnight-hours post with the weekend rotation stated plainly, and reviewer-hour math (4.6 min each, 70 hours, 90 saved) that holds up.
o1.biggest_mistake: The application exercise is a generic angry-customer email with no hidden problem to solve, and the 1/3/5 scale for writing is generic, so reviewers will have little to separate good replies from great ones.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use a realistic exercise with a checkable fix, and write 1/3/5 anchors that fit that exercise.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads like a finished kit: the hard parts come first in the post, there is a time-zone table, the Priya exercise hides a typo in the email address, and it adds a shortlist exercise with a handoff note and set call questions, so the team can run it tomorrow.
o2.biggest_mistake: It gives no offer threshold or decision rule, and the reviewer-hours estimate is thin (first read only, no calibration or second-read time). The word count also runs long.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an offer cutoff and a fuller reviewer-hours estimate, and trim the time-zone table and extras to fit the 1,100-word limit.

reason: Both build on the same signals, but Output 2 hands me a realistic, checkable exercise, specific 1/3/5 anchors tied to it, a shortlist task, call questions and an honest hard-parts-first post I could publish tomorrow. Output 1 has the better decision rule and hours math, but its exercise and scoring anchors are more generic.
